sourceRoutes.evidence: The official PJS article page is indexed with the title, abstract and article text. A prior direct PDF request returned HTTP 403; the PDF was not downloaded or visually reviewed in this step.
sourceRoutes.terms: PJS describes the journal as open access. Its Authors' Guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form. No item-level reuse license for this article was located.

termsFindings: Open Access describes public access without login; it does not by itself grant copyright-free reuse.
Viewing and website-provided downloads are allowed for private study, non-commercial teaching, and non-commercial scholarly research subject to copyright and other restrictions.

Without an explicit item/collection reuse license or written permission, the terms prohibit creating derivative works or structured datasets and prohibit text/data mining or computational analysis of Digital Gems content.
The terms identify NUS Libraries Special Collections as the contact for reuse permissions and computational projects.

limits: Records lack collection dates and coordinates; the locality is text-only.
Existing exact-text GBIF searches for Dampalit Falls and Cambantoc River returned zero; these bounded results do not establish absence.
The records do not substitute for the 2011 survey's multi-site species table or establish a complete Makiling fish inventory.

decision.rationale: The NUS item is accessible for reading, but its terms explicitly restrict structured extraction without an item-level reuse license or written permission. PJS open-access status and its author copyright-transfer policy do not establish an item-specific public data-reuse license. Keep the survey table quarantined.

unsentPermissionInquiry.recipient: NUS Libraries Special Collections (address listed on Digital Gems Terms of Use)
unsentPermissionInquiry.subject: Permission inquiry: structured research use of the 2011 Mt. Makiling fish survey table
unsentPermissionInquiry.body: I am conducting non-commercial research for Bangwit, an independent Philippines fishing-information project. May I manually transcribe the fish names and the paper's species-by-watershed presence cells from the 2011 Paller et al. article into a cited, non-commercial structured research dataset? The proposed fields would be limited to verbatim taxon label, source-reported sampled watershed, publication citation, and an explicit historical period/unknown-date status. I would not redistribute the article PDF, tables, images, or full text. Please advise whether this use is permitted, any required attribution or access/storage conditions, and whether the relevant rights-holder must also grant permission. No data have been extracted pending your guidance.

nextAction: Continue independent, openly licensed, locality-resolved freshwater occurrence discovery in CALABARZON. Keep Molawin as one historical text-locality assertion, and keep Dampalit Falls and Cambantoc River without species rows unless a permitted, independently verifiable source is found.
